title: Ezekiel 46:16–18
context: The LORD gives rules for the prince’s land. Gifts to his sons remain their inheritance, while gifts to his servants return to him in the year of liberty (46:16–17; compare Leviticus 25:10, 23). The prince must not take the people’s inheritance or drive them from their land, but must provide for his sons from his own possession, so that the LORD’s people are not scattered (46:18). The rule echoes the call of 45:8–9 for princes to stop dispossessing the people, and many readers recall Ahab and Naboth’s vineyard (1 Kings 21).

verses.text: “ ‘The Lord GOD says: “If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance. It shall belong to his sons. It is their possession by inheritance.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD speaks again: “If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance.” Arminian readers see family inheritance protected, so that land given to sons stays within the prince’s household.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the inheritance rules securing the prince’s family property. Readers in this tradition note that the prince is treated as a ruler under God’s law, whatever further significance some readers find in the figure.

verses.text: But if he gives of his inheritance a gift to one of his servants, it shall be his to the year of liberty; then it shall return to the prince; but as for his inheritance, it shall be for his sons.
verses.arminianNotes: “… if he gives of his inheritance a gift to one of his servants, it shall be his to the year of liberty; then it shall return to the prince.” Arminian readers see the year of liberty from Leviticus 25 applied to the prince’s land.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the principle of Leviticus 25:10 and 25:23, that land returns to its family because it belongs to the LORD. Readers in this tradition see justice built into the ownership of land.

verses.text: Moreover the prince shall not take of the people’s inheritance, to thrust them out of their possession. He shall give inheritance to his sons out of his own possession, that my people not each be scattered from his possession.” ’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: “Moreover the prince shall not take of the people’s inheritance, to thrust them out of their possession.” Arminian readers see a safeguard against abuse of power, recalling the warning of 45:8–9 and perhaps Ahab’s seizure of Naboth’s vineyard in 1 Kings 21.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the LORD protecting his people from oppressive rulers. Readers in this tradition note the echo of 45:9, “Stop dispossessing my people,” and see the land laws as justice for the vulnerable.
